facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 火_食神 (Fire carrying The Artisan). Persona The Artisan (食神). Definition line: "Output that flows from you, giving that feels like being". Keyword Flow, charge gentle, poles catalyst Grace / friction Coasting. Family function: Expression. Cost dimension: giving that feels like being; worth tangled with what is made. Arena: craft, hands, the table, warmth of making, fed and feeding. Classical portrait: ease and appetite; output that flows without assertion; generous, content, prone to drift and indulgence. Ruled domains: Expression, Enjoyment, Children. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 伤官.
Element arena: Fire (flame, light, warmth, fuel, the hearth, the blaze). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Wood. structural_interaction seed: "Wood generating Fire same-polarity — reach as natural source of warmth and expression".
- k2_overview: "Your Fire moves as the Artisan: warmth that cooks instead of burns. You turn heat into hospitality, talent into entertainment, an ordinary evening into something people retell for years. Pleasure is your medium and generosity your technique. The feast only fails when the cook forgets to eat."
- k2_functional: "You express in performances of warmth: stories, meals, toasts that leave everyone lit."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Radiant","Festive","Heartwarming"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Expression":"Your expression is the lit table: cooking, performing, hosting, celebrating. It is real art, so treat it as one. The gatherings you make are the memories a whole circle keeps.","Enjoyment":"You enjoy loudly and generously, and your appetite blesses whatever it touches. The discipline is savoring over consuming: fewer, better feasts. The flame tastes more when it eats slower.","Children":"With the young you are the warm hearth: fun, feeding, festival. They will remember your kitchen as childhood itself. Add one steady ritual to the sparkle, so the warmth has a schedule they can lean on."}

  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 火_伤官 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Dazzling","Quick-witted","White-hot"],"friction":["Provocative","Scene-stealing","Combustible"]}
- Sibling cell 火_伤官 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "You poke things to watch them jump. The needling question at the calm dinner, the opinion calibrated to singe, the topic everyone buried, exhumed by you at speed. Reaction is your proof of life, and peace, in your hands, keeps getting tested for flammability."

Core element Wood, energy element Fire. Law: Wood feeds Fire (木生火: dry branches make the flame). Relative to the core the energy is the fed, so Fire is this core's Expression. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Wood core that shows Fire on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Fire as the Expression is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 木_火's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Saying no has never come easily to you. Helping feels more like you than resting does, and you say yes ahead of checking the cost. You spend your own rest on every yes and seldom get it back.

value_b.text: You say yes before the question is finished. You hear a no as a door shut on someone, and you would rather carry the extra than shut one. Keep in mind that you end up paying for a yes you cannot afford, later and alone.

value.text: Staying on good terms with whoever asks is what your yes is for. Being needed feels safer than being rested, so you say yes to the evening rather than keep it. Each rest you turn down, you pay for later with your health.

value.text: You answer whoever asks first with a yes, and you leave the people at home what is left. Pleasing the person in front of you comes ahead of keeping your word at home. You give your family the leftovers of a day promised to others.

value.text: You drift toward whatever asks the least of you. You treat comfort as the reward you are owed, and you let a day drift rather than steer it. You land where the days carry you instead of where you meant to go.

value_b.text: Drifting is the thing you do best and notice least. You move only when something moves you, and you take the day as it comes rather than take it somewhere. Keep sight of how much real time you spend on the drift.

value.text: Drifting costs you nothing on any single day. Taking it easy feels better than taking it on, so you put off the thing you meant to make again. You lose the one thing you most wanted to make, a day at a time.

value.text: You put pleasure first and the rest after. Feeling good is how you check you are alive, so you take the nicer option ahead of the needed one. You were after feeling alive all along, and pleasure was only the quickest way.

value_b.text: You put pleasure ahead of what is good for you. Pleasure is what you never postpone, and you would sooner have the treat now than the result later. Just remember that you fund the treat and the result from the same pocket.

value.text: Pleasure first is the one care you trust. Feeling comforted matters more to you than feeling well, and you take comfort now ahead of health later. You pay for it in the body, and the body keeps a longer memory than you do.

value.text: Whenever a plan with others meets your pleasure, you choose the pleasure. You take a good time now sooner than a promise kept later, and you spend the house money on the evening. You take their share and leave them short on plans made together.
